whoWeAre.bannerSub: Your local pharmacy® — independently owned, community driven.
whoWeAre.introPara1: Guardian, I.D.A., and Remedy'sRx pharmacies are independently owned and operated by local pharmacists who dedicate their practice to the best possible patient care — beyond just prescriptions.
whoWeAre.introPara2: With over 1,400 locations coast to coast, both in urban and rural areas, our independent pharmacies reflect the values of the communities they serve. Each pharmacy is unique, but they are all united in the pledge to uphold what being an independent pharmacy stands for — empowering patients to live a healthy life by providing unrivaled, compassionate, holistic health care.
whoWeAre.localPara1: Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy is proud to be part of this tradition — an independent, community pharmacy serving Markham from 9889 Highway 48. Our team gets to know you by name, takes the time to answer your questions, and cares for your whole family, from prescriptions and vaccinations to wellness consultations and health monitoring.
whoWeAre.localPara2: When you walk through our doors, you're not a number — you're a neighbour. That's what being your local pharmacy® means to us.

timeline.title: I.D.A.
timeline.text: The Independent Druggists' Alliance (I.D.A.) is established in Canada, providing exemplary care to patients.

timeline.title: Guardian
timeline.text: The Guardian pharmacy banner is added, with the same unwavering commitment to the profession.

timeline.title: Remedy'sRx
timeline.text: Remedy'sRx is founded with a commitment to building relationships with patients and offering personal attention unmatched by larger chains.

timeline.title: Together
timeline.text: Remedy'sRx joins Guardian and I.D.A. — and together the three brands continue to grow as their independent owners create healthier communities from coast to coast.

whoWeAre.mckessonHeading: Part of the McKesson Canada Retail Banner Network
whoWeAre.mckessonText: While Guardian, I.D.A., and Remedy'sRx pharmacies are independently owned and operated, they are part of a family of banner brands under the McKesson Canada Retail Banner Network. McKesson Canada and its independent pharmacy owners are committed to their communities' better health, partnering with insurers, hospitals, physicians' offices, pharmacies, pharmaceutical companies and governments across the spectrum of care. To learn more, visit www.mckesson.ca.
whoWeAre.disclaimer: Guardian, I.D.A. and Remedy'sRx are banners of McKesson Canada. Pharmacies operating under these banners are independently owned and operated by pharmacists.

blocks.heading: Prescription Transfers
blocks.text: Do you wish to transfer your prescriptions to your local Guardian, I.D.A. or Remedy'sRx pharmacy? Simply fill out our online form to send a transfer request. We'll take care of the rest!

blocks.heading: Medication for Minor Health Problems
blocks.text: If you have a minor health problem (nausea during pregnancy, traveler's diarrhea, lice), you can turn to your pharmacist as a front line health professional. See what they can do for you right away: prescriptions, advice and much more.

blocks.heading: Medication for Chronic Conditions
blocks.text: If you have a chronic condition and require regular medication, your pharmacist is here to facilitate your day to day. They can extend prescriptions and re-prescribe your medication, as well as show you tools to help you get the most out of your treatment.

blocks.heading: Medication Take Back
blocks.text: Cleaning your medicine cabinet? If you have any expired or unused medications, our pharmacists can dispose of it safely and in an environmentally friendly way. Take advantage of this complimentary service by simply visiting your nearest pharmacy.

blocks.heading: Your Medication and Your Safety
blocks.text: Medication should always be taken according to your pharmacist's direction, to avoid incidents. See how you can use and dispose of your medication safely.

blocks.heading: Prescription Renewals
blocks.text: To save time and never miss a dose, you can renew your prescription in advance using one of the following options your pharmacist has made available to you: the mobile app, online renewals, the medication synchronization service and many others.

common_conditions.introHeading: For short-term health conditions, we've got the solution.
common_conditions.introPara1: Are you dealing with a minor or temporary health issue? Your local pharmacist is a valuable resource for treatment and relief.
common_conditions.introPara2: Whether it's alleviating a common cold, managing seasonal allergies, or soothing a mild skin irritation, your pharmacist is there to support your path to better health with the services below.

boxes.title: Prescribing for Common Conditions
boxes.text1: Your pharmacist may be able to assess & prescribe medication for common conditions right in the pharmacy*.
boxes.note: *Conditions apply. Contact your local pharmacy to find out if these services are available.

boxes.title: Ongoing Support & Advice
boxes.text1: Beyond just filling prescriptions, your local pharmacist can enhance your recovery by:
list: demonstrating proper technique and best practices for using the medication
providing education on hygiene practices or lifestyle changes to prevent re-occurrence
advising to see a doctor if the condition doesn't improve with treatment
ensuring you feel comfortable asking questions
medication and allergy records for doctor appointments or travel

long_term_conditions.introHeading: For chronic conditions, we've got the solution.
long_term_conditions.introPara1: Do you have a chronic condition that requires long-term medication and support? Your local pharmacist can be your partner in care throughout your treatment journey.
long_term_conditions.introPara2: Contact your local pharmacy to find out if these services are available.

boxes.title: Monitoring
boxes.text1: Your local pharmacist can play a crucial role in monitoring your medication and overall health. They can help you understand proper dosages, ensure medication adherence, and track medication effectiveness, so that you stay on the right track.
boxes.text2: You can benefit from services that support your chronic condition, including*:
list: Chronic Disease Education
Health screening
Immunizations
Lifestyle advice
Refill reminders
Prescription renewals
Blister Packs
and more

cards.title: Pill-Packs
cards.text1: Using a weekly, bi-weekly or monthly pill-pack can help you organize and take your medication exactly as prescribed. Ask your pharmacist if you can benefit from this service.

cards.title: Simplified Renewals
cards.text1: If you need to renew your medication every month, have your pharmacist set up automatic renewals, so you don't forget. Come pick your medication up every time, at the same time during the month.

cards.title: Synchronization
cards.text1: If you're on multiple medications or manage your family's, why not pick them all at once at the pharmacy once a month? Your pharmacist can synchronize your medication renewals at the same date.

sections.heading: Reminder Tools
sections.intro: With your busy lifestyle and schedule, remembering to take your medication may not rank high in your list of priorities. Fortunately, there are tools that can help you keep on track.

boxes.title: Prescription Extension
boxes.text1: If your prescription is about to expire and you have your medical history on file, your pharmacist can extend it to save you time.*
boxes.text2: This ensures your medication therapy is never interrupted and gives you enough time to book an appointment with your healthcare professional.

medication_safety.introHeading: Use and dispose of your medication safely
medication_safety.introPara1: Medication should always be taken according to your prescriber's direction to avoid medication incidents.
medication_safety.introPara2: Contact your local pharmacy to find out if these services are available.

boxes.title: Returning your Medications Safely
boxes.text1: When was the last time you cleaned out your medicine cabinet? If you look hard enough, you may find expired or unused medications. These could include tablets purchased for prevention of illness during travel, unused pain medications, leftover cough syrup, or outdated birth control pills.
boxes.text2: Do not flush, pour down the sink or throw any of your medications in the garbage. Taking any of these actions can put you, your community and the environment at risk. Instead, visit your nearest pharmacy and let us dispose of them safely on your behalf.

boxes.title: Injections and Needles
boxes.text1: If your medication requires self-injection, your pharmacist can show you the right technique.
boxes.text2: You can also bring back sharp bins at your pharmacy for safe disposal.

cards.title: Step 1
cards.text1: Gather any unwanted or expired prescription medication, over-the-counter medication or natural health products.

cards.title: Step 2
cards.text1: Remove any personal or identifying information from the medication, if applicable. Do not mix medical sharps and medication.

cards.title: Step 3
cards.text1: Find your nearest pharmacy and drop by at your earliest convenience.

cards.tagline: Manage your meds, anytime, anywhere: simple, fast, efficient for regular medication renewals.

cards.title: Online Renewals

cards.text1: With our mobile app, you can renew your medication online, set automatic renewals and even create reminders. You can view the list of all your medications and manage your family's as well. Ask your pharmacist for more information.

cards.title: Medication Synchronization

cards.text1: This service is available for your own prescriptions and your family's. A member of the pharmacy staff will contact you once your prescriptions are due to renew and will walk you through every step. Your pharmacist takes care of everything.

cards.title: Phone

cards.text1: You can renew your prescription directly on the phone. Dial your pharmacy's phone number and talk to a member of the pharmacy staff or leave a message on the automized voicemail. At the pharmacy, ask a pharmacy staff member to help.

vaccinations.bannerSub: Get vaccinated at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy — administered by our pharmacists in a friendly and convenient setting.
vaccinations.introPara1: Vaccination is one of the most effective ways to protect yourself and your family against common diseases. Our pharmacists offer a wide range of vaccination services for children and adults.
vaccinations.introPara2: Whether you're updating your vaccine booklet or preparing for flu season, your MarkhaMack pharmacist is there to help guide you and administer the vaccines so you can focus on what matters most.
vaccinations.vaccinesNote: For more information, speak to your pharmacist.
vaccinations.vaccinesHeading: Vaccines available at our Markham pharmacy
vaccinations.vaccinesIntro: Vaccine availability and funding varies by province and location*. These are the vaccines available in Ontario:
vaccinations.familyIntro: Learn more about vaccines that help shield you against common diseases:

familyCards.title: Flu, COVID-19 & Other Respiratory Viruses
familyCards.text: Vaccination can protect you against different respiratory viruses (flu, COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and pneumococcus). Some vaccines are recommended every year, others only after a certain age.

familyCards.title: Travel Vaccines
familyCards.text: Depending on your destination, some immunizations should be considered before and after your trip for maximum safety. Make sure to book an appointment at least 6 weeks in advance to ensure you are fully immunized.

familyCards.title: Other Diseases
familyCards.text: Vaccination can minimize your risk of contracting several diseases, such as shingles, tetanus, hepatitis and certain childhood illnesses.

other_vaccines.bannerSub: Vaccine-preventable diseases — check with your MarkhaMack pharmacist which vaccines are offered in store.
other_vaccines.introPara1: Vaccination can minimize your risk of contracting several diseases, such as shingles, tetanus, hepatitis and certain childhood illnesses.
other_vaccines.introPara2: These vaccines are available for the general public. Check with your pharmacist if they are offered at our Markham location.

cards.title: Flu
cards.text1: Highly contagious infection of the respiratory tract caused by the influenza virus. Recommended every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone 6 months and older.

cards.title: COVID-19
cards.text1: Infection caused by the constantly evolving SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. Recommended every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 70 and over, or with a weakened immune system or chronic illness.

cards.title: Tetanus
cards.text1: Caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani, which can enter the body through a cut or bite wound.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Hepatitis A & B
cards.text1: Contagious liver infections caused by a virus. The chances of contracting the virus increase when traveling to certain parts of the world.

cards.title: HPV
cards.text1: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a sexually-transmitted virus.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone, as of 3rd grade.

cards.title: Measles
cards.text1: A serious and highly contagious disease, spread through the air when an infected person breathes, coughs, sneezes or speaks.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Children aged 12 to 18 months and all those who have never been vaccinated. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Whooping Cough
cards.text1: Also known as pertussis, a highly contagious disease that causes severe, uncontrollable coughing fits.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Infants aged 2 months and over, and pregnant women. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Pneumococcal Infections
cards.text1: Infections caused by the Streptococcus pneumonia bacteria.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People with a chronic illness or over 65.

cards.title: Shingles
cards.text1: Shingles happen when the virus that causes chickenpox stays in your body and can reactivate at any time during your life.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Ages 18+ for those at increased risk, and ages 50+.

cards.title: RSV
cards.text1: The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a seasonal virus that circulates from fall to spring.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 60 and over.

respiratory_viruses.bannerSub: Vaccination helps you stay healthy and limit the spread of infections — and helps protect your loved ones from serious complications.
respiratory_viruses.introPara1: Vaccination against respiratory viruses helps you stay healthy and limit the spread of infections. By getting vaccinated, you can also help protect your loved ones from serious complications.
respiratory_viruses.introPara2: Talk to your MarkhaMack pharmacist today to schedule your vaccination.

cards.title: Flu
cards.text1: Flu is a highly contagious infection of the respiratory tract caused by the influenza virus. As the virus evolves constantly, it is recommended that you get vaccinated every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone 6 months of age and older; people with a chronic illness, people aged 75 and over, and pregnant women.

cards.title: COVID-19
cards.text1: COVID-19 is an infection caused by the constantly evolving SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. It is therefore recommended that you get vaccinated every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 70 and over, or with a weakened immune system or a chronic illness (e.g. diabetes, heart disease).

cards.title: RSV
cards.text1: The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a seasonal virus that circulates from fall to spring, affecting the respiratory system.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 60 and over.

cards.title: Pneumococcus Infections
cards.text1: These infections are caused by the Streptococcus pneumonia bacteria.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People with a chronic illness or over 65.

sections.heading: Vaccines against respiratory viruses
sections.intro: The following vaccines against respiratory viruses are available to the public. Ask your pharmacist if these vaccines are offered in store.

cards.text1: The flu is much more serious than the common cold and can lead to health complications.
The flu virus changes every year and so does the vaccine. For the best protection, you should get vaccinated every year.
Not everyone is well equipped to overcome the flu. Avoid spreading the flu to your loved ones with a flu shot.
It's easy! Just visit your local pharmacy.

boxes.title: The flu is a serious infection
boxes.text1: The flu is a highly contagious infection that causes symptoms such as fever, cough, muscle aches and severe fatigue. For a healthy person, the flu will cause a lot of discomfort but will usually resolve without complications. For people with health issues, however, the flu can lead to hospitalization or even death. For these people, getting vaccinated every year is a good way to protect themselves against the flu.

boxes.title: Who is most at risk?
boxes.text1: Everyone can get the flu, including healthy adults. In fact, every year, 5-20% of adults will catch the virus. However, some people are at higher risk of flu related complications:
list: People over 65 years old and children under 5 years old
Pregnant women and those planning to become pregnant
Residents of long-time care facilities
People with chronic diseases such as diabetes

travel_vaccines.bannerSub: Your MarkhaMack pharmacist and the planning of your next trip.
travel_vaccines.introHeading: Before you take off, get covered
travel_vaccines.introPara1: If you are planning to travel, it is important to check vaccination recommendations or requirements, as these vary from country to country.
travel_vaccines.introPara2: Pharmacists who offer travel vaccination services can prescribe or administer the required vaccines.
travel_vaccines.introPara3: They can also check that you are up to date with your basic vaccinations and prescribe a booster shot when necessary.
travel_vaccines.introPara4: Consult your pharmacist at least 6 weeks before your departure date to make sure you have the necessary vaccinations and advice.

cards.title: Cholera / Traveller's Diarrhea
list: You visit rural areas with limited access to potable water or where it may not be easy to apply recommended hygiene measures
You are at risk of complications due to any health issues you have

cards.title: Japanese Encephalitis
list: You are planning a trip to a rural area of Asia or Australia

cards.title: Yellow Fever
list: You are planning a trip to Africa or South America
You may require proof of vaccination to enter a country

cards.title: Typhoid
list: You are planning a trip to Asia
You are planning a trip to Africa, the Middle East, or Latin America (especially for long-term stays), where you will visit rural areas or be in close contact with the local population

cards.title: Rabies
list: You could be in contact with bats
You plan to work abroad, and your job involves contact with animals (e.g. animal conservation agent or volunteer in an animal shelter)

cards.title: Hepatitis A & B
list: You will be visiting rural areas with limited access to potable water or where it may not be easy to apply recommended hygiene measures or health standards
You will engage in activities that place you at risk of infection

assessments_monitoring.bannerSub: Always keeping an eye on your progress — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
assessments_monitoring.introPara1: As your partner in health, your pharmacist is not one to simply sit back on good results. They will review your current medication and treatment to further optimize your health outcomes — giving you the right tools to take your health into your own hands.
assessments_monitoring.introPara2: Your pharmacist can prescribe and execute certain tests to make sure your treatment is working for you, and help you keep your condition in check with monitoring tools and advice.

blocks.heading: Diabetes

blocks.heading: Heart Health

blocks.heading: Respiratory Health
blocks.text: If you have asthma or are experiencing strep throat symptoms, talk to your pharmacist about tests to ensure your respiratory health is in order.

diabetes.bannerSub: To keep an eye on your diabetes — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
diabetes.introHeading: To keep an eye on your diabetes
diabetes.introPara1: Whether you have prediabetes, diabetes or are newly diagnosed, many tests exist to ensure your blood sugar is well under control and that your treatment is working well.

cards.title: A1C Test
cards.text1: For pre-diabetics and diabetics, A1C is an important test that indicates if your diabetes is well managed, over a short period of time. This finger prick blood test takes 5 minutes and can be done at any time. Taking this test will help you adjust your treatment to avoid diabetes-related complications.

cards.title: Blood Sugar Readings
cards.text1: You can get your blood sugar readings at your pharmacy. It only requires a quick needle prick on your fingertip. You can then discuss your results with your pharmacist and learn about the best practices to get accurate readings.

cards.title: Self-Monitoring Education
cards.text1: Monitoring your blood glucose is an important part of managing your diabetes. If you wish to use a blood glucose monitor at home, your pharmacist can suggest the best one for your needs and explain how you can use it.

heart_health.bannerSub: To keep an eye on your heart — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
heart_health.introHeading: To keep an eye on your cardiovascular health
heart_health.introPara1: If you are taking medication for your heart, your pharmacist could suggest some tests to determine if your blood pressure or your cholesterol is well managed or to see if adjustments to your treatment are necessary.

cards.title: Hypertension Monitoring
cards.text1: You can get your blood pressure readings done in participating pharmacies using their on-site devices. These results can then be added to your personal health record. With this data, your pharmacist can ensure your medication is doing what it should and that your blood pressure is within normal ranges.

cards.title: Self-Monitoring Education
cards.text1: If you'd rather take your blood pressure in the comfort of your home, you can rely on blood pressure monitors. Your pharmacist can suggest the best practices to get accurate readings and recommend devices that will meet your needs.

cards.title: Anticoagulant Treatment Monitoring (INR)
cards.text1: If you are taking warfarin or anticoagulants, blood tests are necessary to ensure that your anti-clotting medication is on target. Your pharmacist can prescribe this test as needed and adjust your medication. You do not need to have a heart condition to get this test.

cards.title: Cholesterol Monitoring
cards.text1: Getting your cholesterol levels checked is an important step of preventing heart-related diseases and stroke, especially since there are usually no symptoms associated with high cholesterol. Your pharmacist can prescribe this simple blood test if needed and make sure your cholesterol medication is working as it should.

respiratory_health.bannerSub: To keep an eye on your respiratory health — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
respiratory_health.introHeading: To keep an eye on your respiratory health
respiratory_health.introPara1: If you have asthma or are experiencing strep throat symptoms, talk to your pharmacist about these tests to ensure your respiratory health is in order.

cards.title: Spirometry
cards.text1: Spirometry is a simple test that measures how much air flows in and out your lungs. This test can help diagnose certain lung diseases like asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary diseases. This test will also confirm if your treatment is working well and if your condition is under control.

cards.title: Rapid Strep Throat Testing
cards.text1: If you are experiencing symptoms related to a strep throat infection, a nurse will perform this screening test on site to ensure:
cards.text2: Refer to your pharmacist to have your prescription taken care of then.
list: That a bacteria is causing the infection
That antibiotics will be effective

medication_customization.bannerSub: Medication, your way — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
medication_customization.introHeading: Your medication should work for you
medication_customization.introPara1: Sticking to your medication isn't always a walk in the park. Your pharmacist is here to make minor or major adjustments to your therapy or provide you with custom formulas and innovative packaging to make it all easier.
medication_customization.introPara2: When it comes to medication, you can choose how it is given and presented to you. Here's what your pharmacist can do.

blocks.heading: Therapy Adjustments
blocks.text: If you have been taking medication for a while, your pharmacist can adjust your therapy to fit with your needs and lifestyle even more.

blocks.heading: Customized Medication
blocks.text: When it comes to medication, the one-size-fits-all approach does not always cut it. Some medication are available in different formats, sizes, flavours and custom dosages based on your personal preferences.

blocks.heading: Customized Packaging
blocks.text: Like your medication, packaging can also correspond to your needs and situation. Your pharmacist can print larger labels and make sure your bottle is easy to open if you have poor motor skills.

infoBoxes.heading: Compounding
infoBoxes.text: Certain particular health conditions require specific medications, such as a mixture of several medicated creams, which can be prepared at the pharmacy.

infoBoxes.heading: Substituting a brand-name drug with a generic drug
infoBoxes.text: Don't hesitate to ask your pharmacist if a generic version of a prescribed drug exists. A generic drug is pharmaceutically equivalent to a brand-name drug: it contains the same active medicinal ingredients, in the same quantities, in a comparable dosage form.

medication_customization.suggestedSub: Discover our wide range of services offered at our Markham pharmacy

suggestedCards.title: Assessments & Monitoring
suggestedCards.text: Your pharmacist can provide an assessment of your initial therapy and make sure it is the best option for you.

suggestedCards.title: Wellness Consultations
suggestedCards.text: For your pharmacist, your health is also their goal. Turn to them for advice on how to reach your wellness objectives and for private consultations.

suggestedCards.title: Vaccinations
suggestedCards.text: When you need protection against the Flu, common diseases or tropical diseases if you travel, turn to your pharmacist for information and advice.

personalized_medication.bannerSub: Sticking to your medication isn't always easy — we can help, at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
personalized_medication.introHeading: Sticking to your medication isn't always easy
personalized_medication.introPara1: See how your pharmacist can provide your medication according to your personal preferences.

cards.title: Dosage Form
cards.text1: You prefer liquids over pills? Your pharmacist can turn your pills into a liquid formula if possible.

cards.title: Flavour
cards.text1: Some medication tastes bad, but it doesn't have to be that way. Your pharmacist can add a flavour to improve the taste. This can go a long way, especially with children.

cards.title: Pill Size
cards.text1: If your pills are hard to swallow because of their size, ask your pharmacist if they can find a smaller alternative to make things easier.

cards.title: Allergy-Free Formula
cards.text1: If you are allergic to certain components of your medication, your pharmacist can find allergy-free formulations as a substitution.

cards.title: Custom Dose
cards.text1: Your pharmacist can adjust your medication dosage to your needs or preference in order to minimize side effects and optimize results.

cards.title: 1 "Pill" For All
cards.text1: For certain types of medication and conditions (diabetes, hypertension, COPD and asthma), your pharmacist can make sure that some of your medications are combined into one.

personalized_packaging.introHeading: Your medication should work for you
personalized_packaging.introPara1: That applies to the packaging too. Request packaging that meets your needs and preferences.

cards.title: Large-Type Prescription Labels
cards.text1: If you find prescription labels hard to read, ask for our large-type labels to help you read them easily.

cards.title: Easy-to-Open Medication Bottles
cards.text1: If you find it difficult to open your medication bottle, you can ask your pharmacist to provide easy-to-open containers, with lids adapted to seniors and people with poor motor skills.

therapy_adjustment.bannerSub: Your therapy is constantly evolving — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
therapy_adjustment.introPara1: Your medication therapy should be comfortable and suited to your lifestyle. If your medication is the source of undesired effects and interferes with your everyday life, talk to your pharmacist. They may be able to make it more manageable.

boxes.title: Prescription Adjustment & Substitution
boxes.text1: With some adjustments from your pharmacist, side effects can be minimized, harmful drug interactions can be limited and dosages can be decreased in a way that is not detrimental to your well-being.
boxes.text2: If your medication is out of stock, your pharmacist can make sure that your therapy is uninterrupted by making substitutions accordingly.

boxes.title: Medication Review
boxes.text1: Sit down with your pharmacist for a medication review to determine if:
list: Any harmful effects or interactions are caused by combining your medication together
One of your medications can be removed from your therapy
There is a cheaper medication available

wellness_consultation.bannerSub: Healthy body, healthy mind — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
wellness_consultation.introPara1: Your pharmacist truly believes in this. Personalized consultations are available to help you reach your wellness goals or help you navigate life-changing events in health.
wellness_consultation.introPara2: Book a private consultation with your pharmacist to assess your personal situation.

blocks.heading: Pregnancy and Maternity
blocks.text: Looking to get pregnant? Your pharmacist can help you through the whole process until the baby arrives. They will answer your questions related to medication and vitamins, as well as help you relieve pregnancy-related symptoms. They also have breastfeeding equipment to rent.

blocks.heading: Weight Loss
blocks.text: If you're thinking about losing weight, your pharmacist can shed a light on helpful products and make sure your medication doesn't make you gain weight as a side effect.

blocks.heading: Travel Health
blocks.text: Your pharmacist is the key to a healthy trip. All your needs are covered for you to leave with a peace of mind: vaccination depending on your destination, tips on how to travel with medication, advice on essential items to always have on hand.

blocks.heading: Compression Socks
blocks.text: There are many good reasons to use compression socks, whether you have poor blood circulation, want to soothe heavy and tired legs or are planning to take a long flight. Your pharmacist will help you choose the right model, size and material for the best fit possible.

blocks.heading: Smoking Cessation
blocks.text: To stop smoking is not easy. You're not alone; your pharmacist can develop an action plan with you. They can suggest nicotine replacement products (patches, chewing gums, lozenges) and help you deal with withdrawal side effects.

blocks.heading: Mental Health Support
blocks.text: Your pharmacist offers private consultations to discuss your personal progress. They will assess your current medication, talk about alternative options and make sure your side effects are not disruptive. They can act as a bridge between you and your doctor, so you can focus on your recovery.

suggestedCards.text: As your partner in health, your pharmacist can prescribe medication for a minor health problem right away and help you manage the medication you take for a chronic condition.

maternity_pregnancy.bannerSub: Maintain a healthy pregnancy and more — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
maternity_pregnancy.introHeading: Maintain a healthy pregnancy and more
maternity_pregnancy.introPara1: Looking to get pregnant? Your pharmacist can accompany you through the whole process until the baby arrives.

cards.title: Advice on Vitamins
cards.text1: Folic acid plays an essential role in the development of your baby, even before the very first weeks of life. Ideally, you should start taking a supplement at least three months before stopping contraception. Talk to your pharmacist before choosing a product.

cards.title: Advice on Medication
cards.text1: Some medication should be avoided during pregnancy or if you are breastfeeding because they can be harmful to the baby. Before taking any medication, talk to your pharmacist to know more about potential adverse effects. If your little one is in need of OTC medication, your pharmacist can offer advice on the best way to administer it.

cards.title: Pregnancy-Related Symptoms
cards.text1: Nausea and acid reflux are common side effects pregnant women may experience. While they're usually not serious, they can be pretty unpleasant. Your pharmacist can help you manage your symptoms while ensuring there are no risks for the baby.

cards.title: Gestational Diabetes
cards.text1: If you develop gestational diabetes during the course of your pregnancy and must take insulin to control it, your pharmacist will show you how and give you tips on how to manage your condition, including advice on how to monitor your blood glucose at home.

cards.title: Breastfeeding
cards.text1: If you are a new mother, you may need a breast pump. Fortunately, it is possible to rent this device and all its accessories in participating pharmacies. Your pharmacist can also explain how to use it and how to clean your breast pump equipment.

cards.title: App and Home Deliveries
cards.text1: Let your pharmacist come to you: use our app to get your prescriptions prepared ahead of time or to set up home delivery services. This might be useful towards the end of your pregnancy or when your baby is home with you.

smoking_cessation.bannerSub: Your smoking cessation action plan — with Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
smoking_cessation.introPara1: Do you wish to stop smoking? Your pharmacist can provide advice and guide you through this journey. Here's an action plan that you can follow with your pharmacist:

cards.title: Choose a starting point
cards.text1: We all have to start somewhere, so pick a starting date and set achievable goals.
cards.text2: Tell your friends and family and ask them for support.

cards.title: Meet your pharmacist
cards.text1: Your pharmacist will:
list: Determine how dependent you are on nicotine
Help you understand your main smoking habits and identify your triggers
Ask you about your previous attempts to quit smoking to make sure you don't fall back into the same bad habits

cards.title: Follow a personalized treatment
cards.text1: If needed, your pharmacist can prescribe a tailored solution, including:
list: Nicotine replacement products used for replacing the nicotine from cigarettes (patches, chewing gum and lozenges)

cards.title: Reward yourself
cards.text1: You should reward yourself when you're progressing.
cards.text2: Many benefits of a smoke-free life can be felt in the long-term, but some benefits are almost instant as well. So keep on going!

travel_health.bannerSub: Traveling is for everyone — at Guardian MarkhaMack Pharmacy.
travel_health.introPara1: Whether you are hoping to prevent discomfort during your trip, or have a chronic condition that requires medication, your pharmacist has many services that can help. Advise your pharmacist of your travel plans as early as possible to fully benefit from personalized advice.

cards.title: Medication Adjustment for Time Zones
cards.text1: If you are crossing multiple time zones and need to take your medication at a specific time, your pharmacist can make the necessary adjustments to ensure your treatment is uninterrupted.

cards.title: Over-the-Counter Medication Recommendation
cards.text1: Some products are useful to have on hand abroad. From heartburn, allergies or headaches, make sure you have what you need to treat minor health issues.

cards.title: Medication Renewals
cards.text1: You should have enough medication for the duration of your trip, and a bit more just in case of delays. Renew your prescriptions before departure to ensure you don't run out.

cards.title: Medication Prescriptions for Travelers
cards.text1: Your pharmacist can prescribe medication against Traveler's Diarrhea, Malaria and Altitude Sickness depending on your needs and destination.

cards.title: Prescription List & Review for Customs
cards.text1: Get a list of all your medication to clear customs easily and a medication review to ensure all your medications are up to date and safe.

cards.title: Travel Vaccines
cards.text1: Depending on your destination, some immunizations should be considered before and sometimes after your trip for maximum safety.

cards.title: Advice for Travelers with Specific Needs
cards.text1: Travelling while pregnant or with a chronic condition can be intimidating. Ask your pharmacist to recommend which medication and supplies to bring along.

cards.title: Personalized Travel Kit
cards.text1: Questions on mosquito repellent, sunscreen or rehydration solution? Your pharmacist can help you pick the best products for your personalized travel kit.
